transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably nothing major, but... what brings me in is that since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m always up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It's almost like I still have a crew waiting on me to tell them what to do. 

I mean, keeping busy is a good thing, right? I try to stay productive. But I guess I just have a hard time turning it off and relaxing like a retired guy should. Does that make sense? I hope that's the right kind of thing to be coming to you for.
When you're moving from task to task like this, are you also feeling worried or anxious about things, or is it more just a need to stay busy without particular worry?

Oh, no, no, I wouldn't say I'm worried about anything. Life is pretty good, really, and I definitely don't want to sound like a complainer. It's more just... well, just a need to keep moving, I guess. 

Like, if I try to sit down in the recliner to watch a show, my feet just start tapping and I suddenly think about the garage needing sweeping, or the yard... and I just feel a lot better if I get up and do it. I'm not an anxious guy at all. Just... maybe a little too energetic? 

I hope that's a helpful answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it normal to just want to stay on the go like that?
Have you noticed that you're needing less sleep than usual but still feeling full of energy the next day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I still need my sleep, definitely. I try to get my full eight hours every night, just like they say you should. I mean, I might wake up a little early sometimes, ready to get started on the day, but I'm not staying up all night or anything crazy like that. 

I'm pretty good about going to bed at a reasonable hour. I hope that's a good thing? I know some folks my age have trouble sleeping, but I guess I'm lucky that way. Does that sound about right to you?

Thinking back over your life, would you say you've always had this strong drive to stay busy and keep things in order, even before you retired, or is this really a new pattern that started once you stopped working?

Well, I guess... I mean, I've always been a hard worker. You know, you have to be to provide for a family. So, yes, I've always liked to keep things moving and stay on top of my responsibilities. I wouldn't call it a "drive" necessarily, just... being a good employee and a good provider. 

But it definitely feels more noticeable now that I'm retired. When you're working, it's normal to be busy all the time, right? Now that I have all this free time, I guess my body just hasn't gotten the memo that it's okay to sit still. 

I hope that makes sense. I don't want to make it sound like I've always been this restless, but I've certainly always been a doer. Is that the kind of thing you were asking?
Do you find that you have very specific standards for how household tasks should be done, and does it bother you if someone else tries to help but doesn't do it 'your way'?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm difficult about it, or anything like that. My wife, she's wonderful, and she does plenty around the house. I appreciate any help I get, really. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I might, you know, just tidy up after she's folded the towels, just to get the edges perfectly straight. But it's not because I'm upset with her! It's just... well, I have a certain way I like the linen closet to look, and it's just easier if I do it myself so I don't bother her with it. 

I don't make a fuss or anything. I just quietly fix it. That's pretty normal, isn't it? Lots of folks like things a certain way, right? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding like a control freak or anything.
Has this need to have things done just your way ever caused tension in your marriage or other relationships, or made it hard for you to finish a task because it didn't feel perfect enough?

Oh, no, definitely not. I wouldn't say it causes tension. My wife and I, we get along just fine. We've been married a long time, so we know each other's quirks, you know? Like I said, if she does something and it's not quite... well, if I'd prefer it done differently, I just fix it myself. I don't go picking fights over it. I think that's just being a good husband, right? Not making a big deal out of the little things. 

And as for finishing tasks... no, I get things done. I mean, sure, I like to do a good job, and I might take a little extra time to make sure the lawn is edged just right or the garage is swept clean, but I always finish what I start. I don't let things sit half-done just because they aren't perfect. I'd feel terrible leaving a mess for someone else to deal with. 

I think taking pride in your work is a good thing, don't you? I just try to do my best and keep things nice for both of us. I hope that's the right way to look at it.
Do you find that your focus on keeping busy and getting things done leaves little time or interest for leisure activities, hobbies, or spending relaxed time with friends?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I don't have time for leisure. I mean, keeping the house nice and the yard looking sharp, that is sort of a hobby for me now, you know? Some guys play golf, I like to make sure the gutters are clean and the driveway is power-washed. 

I do relax, though! We watch television in the evenings, my wife and I. And we see our friends. We go to church on Sundays and chat with folks there. I just... I guess I'm not the type to sit around playing cards for four hours on a Tuesday afternoon when there's productive things to be done around the house. 

I just like feeling useful, I suppose. It's not that I don't enjoy my downtime, I just prefer to earn it first by getting my chores done. That's a pretty healthy way to look at retirement, isn't it? Staying active and useful? I certainly hope I don't sound like I'm ignoring my friends or anything like that.
Do you ever have trouble getting rid of old tools, parts, or other worn-out items around the house, even when they're no longer useful, because you feel you might need them someday?

Well, I... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble getting rid of things. I mean, my garage is pretty organized, if I do say so myself. 

I suppose I do keep a few extra screws or, you know, maybe a spare piece of PVC pipe here and there. But that's just being practical, right? You never know when a pipe might leak on a Sunday afternoon when the hardware store is closed. It's just smart to be prepared. 

I definitely don't have piles of junk everywhere or anything like that. I like things neat. If something is completely broken and useless, I'll toss it. I just... I like to be resourceful. That's a good quality to have, isn't it? Being able to fix things up around the house instead of having to buy new every time? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.

Would you say you have strict personal rules about matters of right and wrong, or about following procedures 'the correct way,' even in situations where being a bit more flexible wouldn't really hurt anyone?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm strict like that. I mean, I believe in doing things right, of course. If you're going to do a job, you should do it properly, right? But I don't go around enforcing rules on people or anything. 

I just... well, I guess I have my ways of doing things around the house, like I mentioned before. But that's just because experience has taught me the best way to handle certain chores. It's not about being rigid, it's just about being efficient. 

I definitely don't want to come across as some kind of drill sergeant! I try to be easygoing. I mean, if my wife wants to do something her way, that's fine. I might just quietly fix it later if it's really bugging me, but I don't make a fuss. I think it's important to be agreeable, don't you? It keeps the peace. I certainly hope I'm not coming off as stubborn or anything.

When it comes to spending money—whether on yourself, your wife, or the household—would you say you're pretty careful or reluctant to spend, even on things you could easily afford, because you want to save for possible future needs?

Well, I... I wouldn't call myself reluctant, exactly. I mean, we're on a fixed income now, being retired and all, so it just makes sense to be careful, right? You have to watch the pennies so the dollars take care of themselves. 

I certainly don't mind spending money when we need to. If the roof needs fixing, we fix it. And I like to take my wife out for a nice dinner on her birthday, that sort of thing. I just... I guess I'm not the type to go out and buy a brand new sports car just because we have a little extra in the bank. 

I think it's just responsible to have a rainy day fund, especially at our age. You never know when a medical bill might pop up or something. It's just being sensible, isn't it? I definitely don't want you to think I'm a miser or that I don't treat my wife well. I just want to make sure we're secure. That's a good way to manage things, don't you think?

Would you say that this need to keep things a certain way or stay busy ever causes you personal distress, frustration, or gets in the way of your daily functioning or relationships, even if it doesn't cause open conflict?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it causes real distress, no. I mean, I try very hard not to let things get out of hand. But, well, maybe sometimes it gets a little... complicated. 

I guess I do have a habit of forgetting things, or double-booking myself when I'm trying to stay busy. My wife, bless her heart, she's actually had to take over keeping our calendar. She kind of has to check behind me now, just to make sure I'm where I'm supposed to be. It's just easier that way, right? It saves us both a headache. 

And, well, I have had to apologize to the folks at the community center and the community garden group a few times. I've volunteered for things and then just... completely lost track of time or forgot I promised to help. I hate letting people down, I really do. I always try to make it right, though. I just want to be helpful, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm completely unreliable. It's just a little slip-up here and there, which happens to everyone at my age, don't you think?

I'm sorry, did you have another question for me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you everything you need. I hope I'm being helpful so far—I know I can ramble a little bit sometimes. Is there anything else you'd like me to go over? I'm happy to answer whatever you need, doctor.
